claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has moderate hardness and strength together with high ductility.
The starting equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a fully disordered, single-phase solid solution.
The starting alloy lacks nanoscale solute clusters and coherent precipitates.
The absence of nanoscale clusters or coherent precipitates permits relatively easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide causes the favorable plasticity of the baseline alloy.
The absence of fine dislocation obstacles causes the baseline alloy's moderate hardness and strength.
The absence of nanoscale clusters or coherent precipitates limits additional work hardening.
A suitable heat treatment or minor compositional adjustment can induce fine solute clusters or coherent precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi without bulk phase separation.
The induced nanoscale clusters or coherent precipitates will act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Pinning by the induced nanoscale features will increase hardness and compressive yield strength.
Pinning by the induced nanoscale features will reduce plastic strain relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will show an increase of approximately 20% or more in hardness and yield strength.
Microscopy will reveal dislocation interactions and pinning at newly formed nanoscale precipitates.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi under compressive deformation from room temperature through 600 °C.
The hypothesis may not apply when twinning or deformation-induced phase transformations become significant.
